purpose: Define the explicit mutation boundary for canonical semantics so reads, projections, normalization, Topic inheritance/composition, tracing and validation remain side-effect free, while intentional semantic changes are represented as explicit reviewed writes with affected-surface revalidation.

value.name: Validate writable source role
errors: attempt to mutate historical source as active definition

value.name: Trace semantic change impact
outputs: affected canonical identities, Topics, mechanisms, flows and validations

value.name: Unlock affected canonical surfaces
side_effects: affected active contracts marked unlocked where current validation evidence is invalidated

value.name: Revalidate affected canonical surfaces
outputs: new validation evidence and lock eligibility

value.name: Apply and revalidate canonical semantic change

value.mutation_rule: Canonical semantics change only through an explicit semantic write against an authoritative writable definition.
value.derived_edit_rule: A user may edit through a derived UI/projection, but the semantic write must resolve to the authoritative canonical target and canonical operation; the projection itself never becomes the write authority.
value.impact_rule: A semantic change invalidates only validation evidence whose assumptions or trace surfaces are affected, but the affected set must be determined through explicit bidirectional traceability rather than filename/directory heuristics.
value.unlock_rule: Affected previously locked active contracts become unlocked when the change invalidates evidence required for their lock eligibility.
value.revalidation_rule: No affected surface returns to locked until current-format validation produces new sufficient evidence.
value.additive_rule: An additive change still requires impact analysis. Additive does not mean semantically irrelevant.
value.breaking_rule: If a change alters the stable meaning of a semantic identity incompatibly, Semantic Versioning rules require a new identity rather than mutation-in-place.

value.purpose: Group explicit canonical semantic mutation, change impact and revalidation semantics.

invariants.rule: Canonical reads, projections, normalization, Topic resolution, tracing and validation do not mutate canonical semantics.
Semantic writes target explicit authoritative canonical definitions.
Validation evidence invalidated by a semantic change cannot continue to justify locked status.

hard_gates.condition: A projection or derived view directly becomes semantic authority or mutates canonical semantics without resolving an authoritative write target.
Normalization changes the authoritative canonical source.
Topic inheritance or composition resolution changes semantic definitions.
Semantic change is accepted without determining affected canonical surfaces through explicit traceability.
A changed surface remains locked using validation evidence invalidated by the change.
Breaking semantic meaning is changed in-place under an identity that Semantic Versioning requires to remain stable.

references.purpose: Determines authoritative writable versus derived/historical sources.
Affected surfaces require fresh validation before returning to locked.
Changes and revalidation preserve machine-readable provenance/evidence.
Breaking semantic changes require identity-compatible versioning behavior.

semantics.mutation_rule: Canonical semantics change only through an explicit semantic write against an authoritative writable definition.
semantics.derived_edit_rule: A user may edit through a derived UI/projection, but the semantic write must resolve to the authoritative canonical target and canonical operation; the projection itself never becomes the write authority.
semantics.impact_rule: A semantic change invalidates only validation evidence whose assumptions or trace surfaces are affected, but the affected set must be determined through explicit bidirectional traceability rather than filename/directory heuristics.
semantics.unlock_rule: Affected previously locked active contracts become unlocked when the change invalidates evidence required for their lock eligibility.
semantics.revalidation_rule: No affected surface returns to locked until current-format validation produces new sufficient evidence.
semantics.additive_rule: An additive change still requires impact analysis. Additive does not mean semantically irrelevant.
semantics.breaking_rule: If a change alters the stable meaning of a semantic identity incompatibly, Semantic Versioning rules require a new identity rather than mutation-in-place.
